There is a limited amount of research investigating the relative effects of 
gamified elements on student engagement in an eLearning context. Future

2.7 Summary 
In the beginning eLearning began as computer-based training systems, that 
were loaded using CD-ROMs, and now has evolved into online courses. The 
prevalence of eLearning exploded during the dot-com boom. Later during the 
corona-virus pandemic making eLearning became a necessity within the 
classroom, enabling online assessments, lectures and more recently the 
automation of tutoring using AI. 
The recent shift towards eLearning highlights the relevance of creating effective 
tools for students. This projects focus on short-form content, with integrated 
questions, and digital rewards systems aligns with research to increase 
engagement and performance.
